---
title: "Low-pass conditional mixture moments: chr20 calibration and scaling"

  github_document:
    toc: true

## Declaration

The executable declaration is `count_mixture_lowpass/declaration.R`. It is
committed before the campaign it judges. This is a **chr20 point-estimation
and interval-calibration check**, not whole-genome release evidence.

The registered phased 1000G chr20 source, founder pedigree and matched sites
supply linked haplotypes. Sixty CEU and sixty YRI founders are drawn without
replacement with seed 332202610. Each replicate draws distinct founders:
two CEU haplotypes form the sample, two other CEU haplotypes form a
same-population second genome, or two YRI haplotypes form an other-population
second genome. An IBD1 second genome transmits one complete phased haplotype
of the sample and takes its other haplotype from a distinct CEU founder.
Frequencies are the called phased allele frequencies among all founders of
the corresponding population, clamped to [0.001, 0.999]. Founder labels
exclude pedigree descendants; residual relatedness is not independently
screened. Linkage is retained across sites; no genotype-independent SNP
simulation substitutes for phased genomes.

There are 50 replicates in each of 108 primary strata: three relationships,
shares 0/0.01/0.02/0.05/0.10/0.20, depths 0.1/0.2/0.4, and fixed errors
0.0001/0.0002. Depth is Poisson. A fragment independently chooses a source,
then one of its alleles, then has symmetric sequencing error. Equivalently,
ALT is binomial conditional on the two phased dosages. With probability
0.002 a site's ALT count is uniform on 0..depth. Excess homozygosity is zero.
The fitting calibration equals these generating parameters. Matched IBD1
and unrelated hypotheses remain separate conditional fits, not relationship
classification. Blocks are **1 Mb on chr20**, to reach the unchanged
30-informative-block interval floor; no 10 Mb whole-genome precision claim
is made. All statuses, missing intervals and failed fits remain denominators.

The three registered 30x chr20 count tables are thinned at 1/300, 1/150 and
1/75, both as single sources and as ordered two-source combinations at each
nonzero share. Ref and ALT counts are independently binomial-thinned, not
reads or templates. The nominal share is the thinning probability share,
not necessarily the realized fragment share when source depths differ.
Each stratum has 50 draws, fixed error 0.00015, artefact weight 0.002 and
zero excess homozygosity. These are calibration-transfer diagnostics, not
known-truth accuracy gates. Single-source baseline offsets are retained.

### Frozen criteria

Release targets from the design require at least 200 independent replicates
per primary stratum on a genome-wide linked reference. With 50 chr20 draws
these targets are **not evaluated as release gates**, even where a numerical
threshold is met. Observed thresholds are shown separately:

* For correctly specified interior shares at least 0.05: absolute mean bias
  <= 0.005/0.0035/0.0025 at 0.1/0.2/0.4x.
* At least 90% have absolute error <= 0.020/0.014/0.010 for anchored
  other-population singles, <= 0.025/0.015/0.008 for matched unrelated,
  <= 0.050/0.025/0.015 for matched IBD1. Missing fits count as failures.
* Interior 95% interval coverage is 90–98%, counting missing intervals as
  uncovered. Zero-share positive claims use lower limit > 0; their one-sided
  exact 95% binomial upper bound must be <= 0.075. Missing intervals also
  have a separately reported denominator, not an inferred null claim.
* At least one replicate in every synthetic and thinning stratum has all
  native-input block moment sums independently reconstructed in R, with
  exact integer counters and relative error <= 1e-10 (absolute 1e-10 near
  zero). Every primary stratum's first replicate is also fitted at one and
  four threads: statuses must agree and shares and moments must agree to
  the same tolerance.
* Fresh processes, three repetitions each, scale sites 100k/200k/400k and
  sample-by-candidate groups 1/2/4. Peak RSS and DuckDB peak buffers must be
  <= 512 MiB overhead + 3 times modeled live state: 768 bytes per SQL input
  row plus 1024 bytes per physical native block and group. This explicitly
  includes SQL validation/join/sort state, not just bounded native moments.
  Memory limit is 3 GB, no spill. Timing exponent <= 1.25 at each doubling
  is evaluated only if the 1x query takes at least five seconds; smaller
  workloads report timing without a verdict. Input rows, output rows,
  elapsed time, spreads, buffers, RSS and spill remain visible.

The exploratory ordered/unordered/materialization comparison is reported
separately from the declared campaign. Same-population relationship
ambiguity, weak pairs, frequency mismatch and calibration transfer are
limitations, not reasons to drop observations.

## Execution and results

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
source("count_mixture_lowpass/declaration.R")
results_dir <- "count_mixture_lowpass/results"
```

```{r results}
if (!file.exists(file.path(results_dir, "summary.csv"))) {
  cat("Campaign results have not been collected. No criterion has a passing verdict.\n")
} else {
  knitr::kable(read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "summary.csv")))
}
```
